This time, we'll use $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ notation. First, we compute the derivative, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\sqrt{x}-10{x}^{3/4}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{x}^{1/2}-10{x}^{3/4}) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2}-10\cdot \frac{3}{4}{x}^{-1/4} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{x}^{-1/2}-\frac{15}{2}{x}^{-1/4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=16$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=16} & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4}-\frac{15}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{25}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at the point $(16,-60)$ is

$$
m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=16}=-\frac{25}{8}.
$$
